high.title: Fed Chair Delivers Good News for Investors: Hawkish Stance Pulls Down Long-Term Inflation Expectations, 10-Year Yield Falls to 14-Month Low
high.summary:
New Fed Chair Warsh delivered a notably hawkish tone in his first policy meeting, signaling an unambiguous commitment to returning inflation to the 2% target. Fund managers note this has materially reduced long-term inflation expectations — a critical anchor for global rate markets. The US 10-year Treasury yield has fallen from above 2.5% in mid-May to approximately 2.2% this week, its lowest level in over a year. This move is reinforced by a sharp drop in oil prices back to pre-US/Iran conflict levels, alongside the Fed's tighter signaling. Warsh explicitly stated that "persistently elevated prices" are a burden on American households, effectively neutralizing concerns that he would bow to President Trump's repeated pressure for early rate cuts.

**Implications for VND & Vietnam markets:** A falling US 10-year yield and a more credible Fed reduces USD strength pressure globally, which is directionally positive for EM currencies including VND. Lower US yields also reduce the yield differential pressure on Vietnamese government bonds (VGBs), potentially supporting VGB prices. Watch whether the SBV takes advantage of reduced USD demand pressure to rebuild FX reserves. This is the most important global macro input for Vietnam's FX desk this week.

high.title: VN-Index Posts Second Consecutive Weekly Gain; Bank Stocks Show Sharp Divergence — NVB and KLB Lead with +14%
high.summary:
The VN-Index closed the week of June 22–26 at **1,871.91 points**, rising **47.38 points (+2.59%)**, marking its second consecutive weekly gain following a ~33-point advance the prior week. However, breadth remains narrow — gains were concentrated in large-cap names VIC and VHM, while overall market liquidity has not meaningfully improved, a cautionary signal for the sustainability of the rally.

Within the banking sector, performance was sharply divergent: 20 bank tickers advanced while 7 declined. Top performers were **NVB (+14.29%), KLB (+13.95%), LPB (+10.42%), SGB (+9.24%), and SSB (+8.05%)**. NVB (National Citizen Bank/NCB) led the entire banking group, including a single-session limit-up move of +9.38% on June 24, driven by momentum around its large-scale VND 10,000 billion (~USD 390M) private placement — one of the largest such issuances in the sector. On the downside, state-owned banks **VCB, CTG, and BID all closed in negative territory**, alongside EIB (-1.9%) and MBB (-1.0%).

**Implications:** The rally in smaller bank names (NVB, KLB, LPB) appears capital-raising/event-driven rather than a broad re-rating. The underperformance of the Big 3 SOE banks (VCB, CTG, BID) warrants attention — these are typically bellwethers for foreign institutional flows. Foreign fund managers should monitor liquidity trends closely before reading this as a sustainable market re-entry signal. Watch whether the VN-Index can break and hold above the 1,900 psychological level on broader participation.

high.title: Vietnam's Most Critical Banking Regulation to Be Relaxed from Next Week: Lending Room for Real Estate, Infrastructure, and Business Could Expand by Trillions of VND
high.summary: Effective **1 July 2026**, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) will implement Circular 25/2026/TT-NHNN, raising the maximum ratio of short-term funds that commercial banks may use for medium- and long-term lending from **30% to 40%**. The regulation also adjusts the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) framework. This marks the **most consequential banking policy shift in several years** and represents a direct reversal of the progressive tightening cycle that ran from 2019 through October 2023, during which the ratio was incrementally reduced from 40% down to 30%.

medium.title: BREAKING: US Conducts Surprise Strike on Iran Following Hormuz Strait Ship Attack
medium.summary: The US military carried out airstrikes on Iran on June 26 in retaliation for a UAV attack on a cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz the previous day. CENTCOM confirmed strikes on Iranian missile launch sites, UAV positions, and coastal radar stations. President Trump stated Iran had violated a ceasefire agreement. While oil prices have reportedly retreated to pre-conflict levels (as noted in Article 1), an escalation of this nature introduces renewed geopolitical risk premium into energy markets.

medium.title: Green SM of Billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong Receives Over $1 Billion in Capital Since Start of Year; Charter Capital Surpasses SHB and HDBank
medium.summary:
Green SM, the electric taxi and ride-hailing company founded by Vietnamese billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong in March 2023, has raised its charter capital for the fourth time this year — from VND 43,400 billion to VND 54,000 billion (approximately $2.1 billion USD equivalent), as disclosed via a business registration amendment dated June 26. Cash and cash equivalents account for 94.72% of contributed assets. This brings total capital injections since January 2026 to over $1 billion USD. The capital buildup is widely seen as preparation for a planned international IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2027, with advisory valuations suggesting a $20 billion USD price tag — which would make Green SM the first Vietnamese company listed in Hong Kong. While not a direct FX or bond market mover today, this development is worth monitoring: a $20 billion IPO by a Vietnamese company would represent a landmark capital markets event with meaningful implications for USD/VND flows, foreign investor interest in Vietnamese equities, and broader sentiment toward Vietnam's capital markets. The scale of inbound capital flows associated with an eventual IPO could have material FX and liquidity implications.
